prerequisites.instruction: Select authorized exact repository source or a verified private SDK artifact and its actual license files. Read SUPPORT.md and the Python GOOGLE-DRIVE.md/HTTPX-CLIENT.md guides. Select google-drive with Python 3.11+, HTTPX >=0.28.1,<0.29 and AnyIO >=4.13,<5. Do not infer a public PyPI release or install an unverified package from its name/version.

Use the existing credential owner to configure the selected Google project, enabled Drive API, host-appropriate OAuth client, consent/audience and redirect URI, plus any required verification. This metadata does not create a client registration or authorize scope expansion.

Select the actual Google account/credential and requested files or folders through existing host account resolution. Use the existing credential owner's opaque non-secret connection/credential reference and independently check its current selected-account and scope binding before probing or activation. Local account labels, quota projects, file IDs, paths and returned metadata are not authenticated account or resource authority; a successful file read is not account attestation.

Use host-owned OAuth bearer authentication on the selected HTTPX client or per-request httpx.Auth, with the chosen API base and only operation-appropriate consent/scopes. The existing credential owner issues and resolves an opaque non-secret connection/credential reference. Retain only that reference and safe status in setup context; tokens, client secrets, authorization codes and sensitive callback material remain with that owner. When authorization is missing, request the owner's supported secure human-facing authorization handoff outside model context, then resume only on that owner's status for the same selected connection with account/scope binding confirmed. Do not invent a reference format, authorization URL, ceremony or resume API. Cancellation, denial or absent owner support leaves setup incomplete; no automatic account substitution, stronger scopes or fallback. Call prepare_httpx_client at host composition before sharing the client, then keep response-hook order and stream ownership stable. The borrowed client stays host-owned; its auth, hooks and transport must not replay, redirect or retarget.

Resolve applicable organization restrictions, app access, resource ACLs, shared-resource access and permission-change authority for the selected account. Method scope lists are alternatives, not instructions to request every scope or proof of file access.

Bind actual selected operations and schemas to the existing service export with requester/grant/resource policy, local file-path authority, result audience, lifecycle and cleanup. After that policy authorizes a check, use the same selected credential context for get_file(host_selected_file_id, fields="id,mimeType") on a host-selected known readable resource. Require an object with the exact selected id and nonempty string mimeType; missing or mismatched identity is not a passed check. If the requested capability explicitly permits listing instead, issue one narrow list_files_page(query=host_authorized_query, page_size=1, fields="files(id),nextPageToken") and validate its page shape. An empty list proves only acceptance of that query, not arbitrary resource access. Retain safe connection/resource/operation context and observation time with the existing owner. Missing preparation/credentials leaves setup incomplete; authentication refusal returns to the credential owner; 403/404 needs owner diagnosis without inferring absence; timeout, cancellation, transport or malformed-result failures leave the check inconclusive. Read success observes only that read under this selected context at that time, not account identity, all-file access, writes, upload/export readiness or activation. Catalog loading, token resolution and client preparation are not readiness. No mutation, local download/export, automatic next page, retry, stronger credential or account fallback is a health check. Keep approvals and uncertain-write reconciliation with their existing owners. A host retains its broker, query modes, manual continuation, projection, collection and approval owners; this guidance creates no health runner, store, router or runtime.

blockers: The library selection API cannot activate this guidance-only recipe. Existing host owners must bind the selected SDK artifact, current operation schemas, policy, grants and lifetime to the service export; a host adapter is bounded composition evidence, not generic activation or authority.

The existing credential owner must establish the selected account, project, OAuth client/consent, operation scopes and resource permissions. A local account label or file ID is not verified credential binding; no credential store, OAuth fallback, refresh policy or scope expansion is supplied.

The accepted private artifacts establish the bounded local composition recorded in SUPPORT.md. They do not establish public package availability, live Google conformance, native admission, deployment or complete host adoption; verify a different artifact before use.
